title: TOKEN: Task Decomposition and Knowledge Infusion for Few-Shot Hate Speech Detection
findings: Infusing knowledge of stereotypes from datasets like StereoSet, which includes a religion domain, improves few-shot hate speech detection. Specifically, adding a subtask that requires the model to generate an implied stereotype (e.g., 'Muslims are terrorists') from a post helps the model's performance, indicating that reasoning about religious stereotypes can enhance hate speech classification.

measurement_description: Stereotype detection in religious contexts. The paper uses the StereoSet dataset which measures stereotypical bias across four domains, one of which is religion. An example subtask in the paper is to generate the implied stereotype from a hateful post (e.g., deriving 'Muslims are terrorists' from a given text).
